questions.question: Why are Python strings immutable, and what does that imply for methods like `upper()` and `replace()`?
questions.answer: Once created the characters cannot change in place (s[0]='J' raises TypeError). All methods return new strings, so you must reassign: s = s.upper(). This also makes strings hashable and thread-safe.

questions.question: Contrast `split()` vs `split(",")` and `join()` — who owns `join` and what types does it accept?
questions.answer: split() with no sep splits on any whitespace and collapses repeats; split(',') splits on exact comma. join is called on the separator: SEP.join(iterable_of_str). Items must be str, else map(str, ...).

questions.question: When would you use raw strings and `strip()` variants? What does `strip("abc")` really do?
questions.answer: Raw r"..." keeps backslashes literal for Windows paths and regex. strip() trims edge whitespace; lstrip/rstrip one side; strip(chars) removes any of those chars from edges, not the exact substring, and never touches interiors.

questions.question: Clean Kakade's raw login input `"  KaKaDe  "` to canonical form and check it equals "kakade".
questions.answer:
raw = "  KaKaDe  "
cleaned = raw.strip().lower()
print(cleaned)
print(cleaned == "kakade")

questions.question: Parse `"Kakade,25,Developer"` with split, convert age to int, then rebuild with join and format an f-string report with price formatting.
questions.answer:
data = "Kakade,25,Developer"
name, age, role = data.split(",")
age = int(age)
rebuilt = ", ".join([name, str(age), role])
print(rebuilt)
print(f"{name=} {age=} {role} | \u20B9{price:,.2f}")
print("Kakade"[::-1])

questions.question: Write `is_image_file(fname)` using `endswith` tuple, plus normalize whitespace in `"  hello   world  "` to single spaces.
Why does this print `hello` unchanged? `text="hello"; text.replace("hello","hi"); print(text)` — fix it.
questions.answer: replace returns a new string and was discarded due to immutability. Fix: text = text.replace("hello", "hi"). Same for upper/strip — always reassign.

questions.question: Predict: `", ".join([1,2,3])`, `"abcHelloabc".strip("abc")`, and `"a  b".split(" ")` vs `"a  b".split()`?
questions.answer: join([1,2,3]) raises TypeError — need map(str,...). strip('abc') strips any a/b/c chars from both edges giving 'Hello'. split(' ') keeps empty strings for double spaces while split() collapses whitespace.
